title: Clarinet
summary: Performance files exist for every normal-set fingering of a published 1981 Buffet Crampon Prestige bore and tone-hole lattice, blown at the published mezzo-forte mouth pressure and observed at the physical baffled outlet receiver. They have not been built or rendered yet, so nothing here is graded. The specimen is a population proxy for the UIowa R13, not the same instrument.
physics_present: fs-duct transfer-matrix air column built from the published Taillard and Sanchez 2016 bore station table, split at every chimney and never decimated, with the Vandoren M30 exit cone
every tone hole as a side branch (published position, minimal diameter and chimney height); the Moers and Kergomard 2011 normal-set chart decides which are open
flanged radiation load at the bell and the physical baffled outlet receiver for the radiated pressure (not the listener_m proxy)

lumped single-reed Bernoulli aperture with lay contact from the shared reed owner, driven by a mezzo-forte mouth pressure program interpolated from Fuks and Sundberg 1996 (two professionals on a Buffet Crampon Prestige)
physics_missing: the reed opening, width, closing pressure and damping are the authored BR-04 constants, not a measurement of this reed and mouthpiece; the reed is quasistatic, so reed resonance and mass are not in the loop
the mouthpiece chamber, baffle, throat and lay are unknown; the cavity is an equivalent cylinder matched to the published internal volume and length
open tone holes do not radiate in the observer (only the bell does), and undercuts, pad geometry and key rise are unknown
dry room-temperature air everywhere: the warm humid breath field is not applied
no wall vibration, no player airway, lips or tongue, and no vibrato
the specimen is not the UIowa Buffet R13 and no same-specimen passive comparison exists yet; fingerings outside the normal set have no chart
